chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Jahm, from Rifā'ah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Girrith, and he said: 'By Allah, I have never seen it, but we found it in the book of Ali (peace be upon him) as forbidden (haram).'

key_terms.الجِرَّيۡثِ: Girrith, a specific type of fish or aquatic creature mentioned in hadith
key_terms.حَرَاماً: Forbidden, a legal ruling indicating prohibition
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali, referring to a collection of rulings attributed to Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Girrith in Shia jurisprudence according to the book of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* highlights the transmission of specific legal rulings through the Ahl al-Bayt, where Imam al-Sadiq (a) relies on the authoritative written record of Imam Ali (a) rather than personal observation. It underscores the Shia scholarly principle that the Imams' knowledge is rooted in the inherited wisdom and texts of their predecessors, establishing the prohibition of the 'Girrith' as a transmitted legal fact.
